sources.title: ICC Assets (calibration and maintenance) module page
supportedClaims: The published ICC page describes an equipment register in which each piece of equipment carries its calibration interval and attached certificates, with status labels such as due soon and in date. These are published descriptions; availability and configuration must be confirmed in a demonstration and no capability is advertised as verified.
The page describes a calibration record showing that calibration was recorded, a certificate attached and the next due date set.
The page states the register can be loaded in bulk from Excel; it gives no detail on how the import works.
The page states maintenance is recorded against the same equipment record.
The page describes inspection checklists built once and scheduled as programmes, with performed and reviewed e-signatures on inspection records.
The page describes QR labels on equipment that open its record on the shop floor, and PIN access for people without a desk login.

The page describes an auditor view showing the equipment register with calibration status and next due date, certificates attached to each instrument, completed inspection records with both signatures and timestamps, and maintenance history for each asset.
The page maps the module to ISO 9001:2015 clauses 7.1.5 and 7.1.3, ISO 13485:2016 clause 7.6 and ISO/IEC 17025:2017 clause 6.4; a mapping is not a statement that software alone satisfies a clause.

The page describes setup with the vendor: processes mapped, modules configured, standards onboarded and training included, with a certified consultant reviewing the configuration through to the audit.
The page states every AI output is a suggestion that a person reviews before it enters a controlled record.
The page does not state due-date alerts or reminders, pricing, or how the register import works; those are evaluation questions.

sources.title: Metrological Traceability: Frequently Asked Questions and NIST Policy
sources.publisher: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST)
supportedClaims: NIST adopts the VIM definition (JCGM 200:2012, 2.41): traceability is the property of a measurement result whereby the result can be related to a reference through a documented unbroken chain of calibrations, each contributing to the measurement uncertainty.
Traceability is a property of a measurement result, not of an instrument, report or laboratory; merely having an instrument calibrated is not enough to make a result traceable.

The chain must be a complete, explicitly described and documented series of calibrations linking the result to each intermediate reference and to the highest reference claimed, and each link contributes to the measurement uncertainty.
Each link needs a defined measured property, a description of the measurement system and a specification of the reference used; the reference is typically a national or international standard.
Internal measurement assurance programs must establish the status of the measurement system and the reference at the relevant times.

The provider of a result is responsible for supporting its traceability claim and the user is responsible for assessing that claim; the provider must document the process and chain so a user can assess it.
Traceability does not signify or guarantee fitness for purpose; results can be traceable yet have uncertainty too large for a given use.
Using a standard reference material does not by itself make a user's results traceable; the user must document an unbroken chain and an assurance program.
Laboratory accreditation shows competence; it does not certify the traceability of a specific result.
NIST certifies traceability only for results it provides itself and does not certify the claims of others.

sources.title: ISO 9001 Auditing Practices Group
supportedClaims: The Auditing Practices Group was established in 2003 as an on-line source of papers on auditing quality management systems; it is an informal group drawn from ISO/TC 176 and the IAF.
The papers are non-definitive and are not required criteria for an audit.
The page lists papers titled Monitoring and measuring resources and Measurement traceability under auditing to ISO 9001:2015; this page does not summarize their content.

An August 2024 news item on the page says the resources paper was revised, that resources are a key element of a quality management system, and that auditors should consider how the resource requirements in clause 7.1 relate to other requirements.
The page does not discuss calibration intervals, software or documented information.

mapping-workflows.title: Map the calibration decision for every instrument
mapping-workflows.description: Mapping the current workflow in calibration management software: define the problem, trace records and handoffs, assign owners and set acceptance criteria.
boundaries: Map the existing calibration decisions and handoffs; leave register design to the instrument register chapter.
Leave vendor comparison to the evaluation chapter and migration mechanics to the migration chapter.

subsections.title: Start with the instrument that cannot be found
keyPoints: Name the question a quality lead must answer: which instruments are in use, which are in date and which have evidence on file.
The auditing papers on the ISO/TC 176 Auditing Practices Group page are non-definitive; treat them as context, not required criteria.

workflow.input: Floor walk list, existing spreadsheets and paper certificates
workflow.decision: Decide which instruments belong in scope and which are excluded with a reason
workflow.record: Scope list with owner and reason for each exclusion
workflow.exception: An instrument is in use but appears in no list

evaluationCriteria: Can the team name every instrument in scope, its owner and where its latest certificate sits without searching?
subsections.example: A supervisor finds a gauge at a workstation that appears in no spreadsheet and records it as a scoping gap.

subsections.title: Trace records and handoffs
keyPoints: Map the path from calibration request to returned instrument, certificate review and updated due date.
NIST describes traceability as a documented unbroken chain of calibrations; the workflow map should show where that documentation is created and stored.

workflow.input: Calibration requests, supplier certificates and internal check records
workflow.decision: Accept the certificate and release the instrument, or hold it
workflow.record: Handoff log from sender to reviewer to releaser
workflow.exception: Certificate returns late or incomplete

evaluationCriteria: Does the map show who receives the certificate, who reviews it and who releases the instrument?
subsections.example: The coordinator notes that certificates arrive by email at one desk and are filed by another person weeks later.

subsections.title: Assign owners and set acceptance criteria
keyPoints: Assign an instrument owner, a certificate reviewer and a back-up for each calibration decision.
Define in advance what counts as an acceptable workflow: every in-scope instrument has an interval, a certificate and a next due date.

workflow.input: Instrument list, role list and absence cover
workflow.decision: Approve ownership and the acceptance criteria
workflow.record: Owner assignments and the signed-off acceptance criteria
workflow.exception: Owner absent or role vacant

evaluationCriteria: Can a vendor demonstration be judged against written acceptance criteria rather than impressions?
subsections.example: The team writes three acceptance criteria and a back-up reviewer for the inspection instruments.

mapping-workflows.scope: Cover the current-state calibration workflow, ownership and acceptance criteria.

evaluating-software.title: Evaluate calibration management software against real instruments
evaluating-software.description: Evaluating software capabilities in calibration management software: build a workflow shortlist, test decision points, examine evidence and compare support.
boundaries: Evaluate fit using the mapped workflow; do not design the register fields here.
Do not describe unverified ICC features as confirmed; frame them as demonstration questions.

subsections.title: Build a workflow-based shortlist
keyPoints: Score each candidate against the mapped workflow and acceptance criteria rather than a feature list.
The ICC page describes an equipment register, calibration records, maintenance history and an auditor view; confirm each in a demonstration.

workflow.input: Mapped workflow, acceptance criteria and candidate list
workflow.decision: Shortlist candidates that can show the whole decision path
workflow.record: Scoring sheet with evidence from each demonstration
workflow.exception: A candidate cannot show a required step

evaluationCriteria: Does every shortlisted candidate demonstrate the steps from the workflow map, in order?
subsections.example: The team asks each vendor to run one instrument from due date to released certificate.

subsections.title: Test the decision points
keyPoints: Ask the vendor to show a certificate review, an out-of-tolerance decision and a missing certificate.
The ICC page does not state due-date alerts or reminders; ask whether and how due dates trigger action.

workflow.input: Sample instruments, a sample certificate and an incomplete record
workflow.decision: Accept, reject or defer the candidate on observed behavior
workflow.exception: A required decision path cannot be shown

evaluationCriteria: Can the vendor show what happens when a certificate is missing, not only when everything is complete?
subsections.example: The team brings one instrument with no certificate and asks what the register shows.

subsections.title: Examine evidence, access and support
keyPoints: Check what an auditor sees, who can edit calibration records and how changes are traced.
The ICC page describes QR labels, PIN access for people without a desk login and a vendor-led setup; the page gives no pricing, so ask in writing.

workflow.input: Access list, support questions and price request
workflow.decision: Select the candidate whose evidence, access and support terms fit
workflow.record: Written vendor answers on access, support and cost
workflow.exception: Vendor answers are vague or verbal only

evaluationCriteria: Are access rules, support scope and cost confirmed in writing before the decision?
subsections.example: The team requests the support scope and import details in writing before shortlisting.

evaluating-software.scope: Cover vendor evaluation using the workflow map, with ICC claims as demonstration questions.

subsections.title: Define the register record
keyPoints: Each equipment record carries its calibration interval and attached certificates on the ICC page; decide which other fields the team needs.

workflow.input: Instrument list, supplier details and procedures
workflow.decision: Decide the mandatory fields for each instrument class
workflow.exception: Instrument class has no agreed interval

evaluationCriteria: Can every instrument be identified and its interval found from one record?
subsections.example: The team lists identification, location, owner, interval and certificate as the minimum fields.

subsections.title: Set intervals and ownership
keyPoints: Set each interval deliberately and record the reasoning; the NIST page notes that traceability does not guarantee fitness for purpose.

workflow.decision: Confirm or adjust each interval

evaluationCriteria: Does the register show why an interval was chosen and who may change it?

subsections.title: Attach and identify the certificate
keyPoints: The ICC page describes a calibration record with a certificate attached and a next due date set.
Link each certificate to one instrument and one calibration event.

workflow.decision: Attach the certificate or return it to the supplier
workflow.exception: Certificate lacks an instrument identifier

evaluationCriteria: Can a certificate be traced to exactly one instrument and one event?
subsections.example: A certificate that does not match an instrument serial number is held for correction.

subsections.title: Check what traceability means
keyPoints: NIST defines traceability as a property of a measurement result, linked to a reference through a documented unbroken chain of calibrations, each contributing uncertainty.
Having an instrument calibrated is not by itself enough to make a result traceable.

workflow.input: Certificate, reference information and uncertainty statements
workflow.decision: Accept the evidence or request more
workflow.record: Review record with the chain evidence checked
workflow.exception: Chain is incomplete or uncertainty is missing

evaluationCriteria: Does the review step prompt the reviewer to check the chain and uncertainty, not only the date?
subsections.example: The reviewer asks the supplier for the missing uncertainty statement before accepting.

subsections.title: Decide acceptance and fitness for use
keyPoints: NIST states traceability does not guarantee fitness for purpose, so record the check that the result suits the use.
Keep reviewer identity and decision with the certificate.

workflow.input: Certificate, tolerance requirements and intended use
workflow.decision: Accept for use, restrict or reject
workflow.exception: Result is traceable but too uncertain for the task

evaluationCriteria: Does the record show who accepted the certificate, when and for which use?
